When we write an expression like $\maroonD{7}^\blueE{2}$, we call $\maroonD{7}$ the $\maroonD{\text{base}}$, and we call $\blueE{2}$ the $\blueE{\text{exponent}}$.

The $\blueE{\text{exponent}}$ tells us how many factors of the $\maroonD{\text{base}}$ we should multiply to find the value of the expression.

For example, $\maroonD{4}^\blueE{3} = \maroonD{4} \cdot \maroonD{4} \cdot \maroonD{4}$ and $\maroonD{5}^\blueE{4} = \maroonD{5} \cdot \maroonD{5} \cdot \maroonD{5} \cdot \maroonD{5}$.
